maria: Heads-up — we just received a DSAR from a EU requester asking for account + conversation erase and proof of deletion. They uploaded PDFs and reference a different email than the account on file. Do we have an approved verification flow for when requester email != account email? cc @legal-ops
elliot: If email mismatches, follow Legal's verification checklist. Ask for government ID + one account-specific artifact. Also confirm there's no legal hold. For infra side we need to track vector DB + snapshot deletes.
samir: From infra: deletion surfaces are S3 snapshots (encrypted), vector DB instances, and our metadata index that references KMS-wrapped pointers. Standard flow: verify identity -> run privacy-export -> purge vector entries -> delete S3 objects -> confirm KMS access logs. If email != account, require relationship proof (e.g., HR ticket).
legal-ops: Confirmed — no legal hold on this user. Verification: gov ID (photo), plus one of: last 4 CC on file OR support ticket id that included account email. If they provide a company email explaining relation, we need an additional attestation.
maria: One wrinkle: keystore rotation happened last week. If objects are encrypted under an old key, do we need to decrypt to generate content-level proof before deletion? Concern is we can't produce a hash of content if we never decrypt.
samir: Good catch. Deleting encrypted blobs is fine for removing access, but producing a content hash for proof requires decrypting under the old KEK. We keep key rotation metadata (old key IDs). Ops can perform a controlled decrypt/export for proof generation, then re-delete. That action requires short-lived decrypt perms and must be logged.
security-bot: Tip: run `/privacy-export <DSAR_ID>` to produce a proof bundle. Bundle contains: S3 object manifest, vector purge logs, KMS key IDs, and time-ordered audit entries. Make sure to upload bundle to the DSAR ticket.
elliot: RBAC request: the engineer running the export needs KMS decrypt + S3 read for the export window. Recommend ephemeral role `privacy-erasure-operator` with STS token TTL=1h and recorded justification. Can we automate minting?
samir: We have an STS flow. I'll draft a Terraform snippet and a short-runbook for manual issuance. We will ensure IAM grant events show up in audit. Example snippet I plan to use:
```hcl
resource "aws_iam_role" "privacy_erasure_operator" {
  name = "privacy-erasure-operator-${var.project}"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.assume_role.json
}
```
This role will be timebound and annotated with `dsar=<id>` tag.
maria: Thanks. Also the requestor claims a prior support rep granted a retention exception allowing data to be kept 90d. They now retract and ask for erasure. How do we ensure exceptions don't block deletion?
legal-ops: Retention exceptions must be logged in Compliance's registry. If an exception existed, Compliance revokes it and triggers deletion workflows. If you see an exception, escalate to Compliance immediately; they will clear the exception and authorize purge.
elliot: Action items: 1) Samir — draft ephemeral role + terraform + runbook. 2) Maria — collect verification artifacts from requester and attach to ticket. 3) Legal — confirm no hold and clear exception if present. 4) Security — run `/privacy-export` and attach proof bundle; capture KMS logs. I'll book a 30m runbook for handoff once export is ready.
maria: I'll collect artifacts now and will post once done. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
